title: Nagoya Castle & the Fastest Train on Earth
description: Nagoya Castle's golden shachihoko, then the SCMAGLEV and Railway Park — Japan's train history including the world's fastest maglev (603 km/h). Perfect for a family that loves things that go fast.

activities.title: Nagoya Castle
activities.description: One of Japan's most important castles, famous for golden shachihoko roof ornaments. The reconstructed Honmaru Palace is a masterpiece of traditional architecture.
details: 🏯 Honmaru Palace — hand-painted fusuma sliding doors throughout
📸 Golden shachihoko are Nagoya's symbol
🎫 ¥500 entry · Open 9am-4:30pm

tips.text: The Honmaru Palace is the real star — the interior craftsmanship is jaw-dropping.

activities.title: SCMAGLEV and Railway Park
activities.description: JR Central's incredible train museum. Walk through retired Shinkansen, steam locomotives, and the actual maglev test vehicle that hit 603 km/h. The simulator experiences are a must.
details: 🚄 39 real trains on display — Shinkansen, steam, electric
🧲 MLX01 maglev — the world speed record holder at 603 km/h
🎮 Shinkansen driving simulator — feels incredibly real
👶 Kids' play area with mini trains to ride
⏰ Allow 2-3 hours
🎫 ¥1,000 · 📍 Kinjofuto Station (Aonami Line)

meals.name: Misokatsu — Yabaton
meals.description: Nagoya's famous miso-glazed tonkatsu. Thick, crunchy pork cutlet drenched in sweet-savory red miso sauce. Yabaton is the classic chain.

activities.title: Farewell Nagoya Night
activities.description: Last evening in Nagoya — revisit your favorite food street or explore a new area. Consider the Noritake Garden (ceramics museum) if time allows.

meals.name: Taiwan Ramen — Misen
meals.description: Nagoya's unique Taiwan ramen — spicy ground pork, garlic chives, and fiery chili. Not actually from Taiwan, 100% Nagoya original.

title: Back to Tokyo — Toyosu & Roppongi Hills
description: Return to Tokyo by Shinkansen. Visit the new Toyosu Fish Market (where Tsukiji's inner market moved), then spend the evening at Roppongi Hills for art and city views.

activities.title: Shinkansen Back to Tokyo
activities.description: 1h40 on the Hikari from Nagoya back to Tokyo Station. Quick, comfortable, and scenic.
details: 🚅 Covered by JR Pass on Hikari
🍱 Last chance for a Nagoya ekiben — try the tenmusu (tempura rice ball) bento

activities.title: Toyosu Fish Market
activities.description: The massive new fish market that replaced Tsukiji's inner market. Watch the famous tuna auction (from a viewing gallery), browse the wholesale area, and eat the freshest sushi in the world.
details: 🐟 Tuna auction viewing gallery opens at 5:30am (if you're ambitious)
🍣 Restaurant row — incredible sushi, sashimi, and seafood donburi
📸 Watch the fish merchants in action from elevated walkways
⏰ Restaurant lunch rush is 11am-1pm — arrive at 10:30 or after 2pm

meals.name: Sushi Dai (Toyosu)
meals.description: The legendary sushi counter that moved from Tsukiji. The omakase (chef's choice) set is life-changing. Expect a 1-2 hour wait, or try nearby alternatives.

activities.title: Roppongi Hills & Mori Art Museum
activities.description: One of Tokyo's most impressive urban complexes. The Mori Art Museum on the 53rd floor combines contemporary art with the best observation deck in Tokyo — Tokyo City View.
details: 🎨 Mori Art Museum — rotating contemporary exhibitions
🌃 Tokyo City View observation deck — 360° panorama at 250m
🗼 Sky Deck (rooftop, weather permitting) — open-air views of Tokyo Tower
🛍️ Roppongi Hills shops and restaurants below

meals.name: Butagumi Roppongi
meals.description: Premium tonkatsu (pork cutlet) restaurant specializing in heritage pork breeds. You choose your cut and breed — each has different flavor and texture.

mapPins.label: Toyosu Fish Market
mapPins.desc: World's biggest fish market — tuna auctions and sushi

mapPins.label: Roppongi Hills
mapPins.desc: Mori Art Museum and Tokyo City View

mapPins.label: Tokyo Tower
mapPins.desc: Iconic 333m broadcast tower — visible from Roppongi

neighborhoods: Yokohama · Minato Mirai · Cup Noodles Museum
title: Yokohama Day — Cup Noodles & Chinatown
description: Day trip to Yokohama — Japan's second city, just 30 minutes from Tokyo. Visit the Cup Noodles Museum (make your own!), explore the massive Chinatown, and see the gorgeous Minato Mirai waterfront.

activities.title: Cup Noodles Museum
activities.description: The interactive museum celebrating instant noodles inventor Momofuku Ando. The highlight: design your own Cup Noodles package and choose your toppings from scratch.
details: 🍜 My Cup Noodles Factory — design your own cup and pick toppings (¥500)
🎨 The cup you design is a perfect souvenir
👶 Chicken Ramen Factory — make noodles from scratch by hand (book ahead)
⏰ Opens 10am, arrive early for My Cup Noodles (popular during holidays)

tips.text: Book the Chicken Ramen Factory in advance online — slots fill up fast. The My Cup Noodles section is first-come-first-served.

activities.title: Yokohama Chinatown
activities.description: The largest Chinatown in Japan (and one of the biggest in the world) — over 500 shops and restaurants packed into colorful streets. The food is incredible and the energy is electric.
details: 🥟 Shoronpo (soup dumplings) are the specialty — try them everywhere
🏮 Ornate gates and temples throughout
🐉 Kanteibyo Temple — elaborate Chinese temple, free entry
🛍️ Souvenir shops, fortune telling, and panda-themed everything

activities.title: Minato Mirai Waterfront Walk
activities.description: Yokohama's modern waterfront district — skyscrapers, the iconic Cosmo Clock ferris wheel, and gorgeous bay views. Great for a family stroll.
details: 🎡 Cosmo Clock 21 — one of the world's largest ferris wheels
🏢 Landmark Tower — observation deck on the 69th floor
🚢 Red Brick Warehouse — shops and restaurants in a historic warehouse
📸 The waterfront promenade at sunset is stunning

meals.name: Yokohama Chinatown Crawl
meals.description: Graze through Chinatown: soup dumplings, char siu bao, peking duck wraps, sesame dango, and bubble tea.

activities.title: Return to Tokyo & Shimokitazawa
activities.description: Head back to Tokyo and explore Shimokitazawa — Tokyo's coolest neighborhood. Vintage shops, live music venues, tiny cafés, and a bohemian vibe completely different from the rest of Tokyo.
details: 🎸 Live music venues — check what's playing tonight
☕ Specialty coffee shops everywhere
👗 Vintage clothing stores — some of Tokyo's best
🍺 Craft beer bars and natural wine spots

meals.name: Shirube Shimokitazawa
meals.description: A tiny, atmospheric izakaya with seasonal Japanese dishes, local sake, and a warm neighborhood vibe. The kind of place you'll wish existed near your home.

mapPins.label: Cosmo Clock 21
mapPins.desc: Giant ferris wheel on the waterfront

title: Last Full Day — Hidden Tokyo & Up Garage
description: Your final full day in Tokyo. Hit the spots most tourists miss: Nakano Broadway (the real otaku paradise), Up Garage for JDM parts shopping, and one last epic Tokyo night.

activities.title: Nakano Broadway — The Real Akihabara
activities.description: Where serious collectors shop. Four floors of tiny shops selling vintage toys, rare anime figures, retro games, and — crucially — incredible JDM car collectibles that you won't find in touristy Akihabara.
details: 🏎️ Mandarake stores — rare die-cast cars, vintage car manga, racing memorabilia
🎮 Retro game shops with better prices than Akihabara
🧸 Vintage toy stores — find treasures from the 80s and 90s
💎 Less crowded and more authentic than Akihabara

meals.name: Chatei Hatou (Shibuya)
meals.description: One of Tokyo's most legendary kissaten (vintage coffee shops). Hand-dripped coffee in a wood-paneled room unchanged since 1979. A perfect quiet moment.

activities.title: 🏎️ Up Garage — JDM Parts Shopping
activities.description: The ultimate used JDM parts chain. Wheels, body kits, exhausts, interior parts — all from real Japanese cars. Even if you can't ship parts home, browsing is incredible. Check multiple locations for the best finds.
details: 🛞 Used Rays, Volk, Work, BBS wheels — way cheaper than overseas
🔧 Performance parts: HKS, Trust, Blitz exhausts and turbos
💺 Recaro and Bride seats, Nardi and Momo steering wheels
📦 Some locations can arrange international shipping
📍 Check Up Garage website for nearest locations with your desired parts

activities.title: Ikebukuro Sunshine City
activities.description: A massive entertainment complex with an aquarium, planetarium, shopping, and Pokémon Center. Great for families — the Sunshine Aquarium on the rooftop is unique.
details: 🐠 Sunshine Aquarium — penguins fly overhead in sky tunnels
⭐ Konica Minolta Planetarium — stunning shows
🛍️ Pokémon Center Mega — the biggest Pokémon store in Tokyo
🎮 Namja Town — indoor theme park with gyoza stadium

meals.name: Ramen Street (Tokyo Station)
meals.description: Eight of Japan's best ramen shops in one underground corridor at Tokyo Station. Tonkotsu, miso, shoyu, tsukemen — pick your fighter.

activities.title: Shinjuku Golden Gai — Farewell Night Out
activities.description: End your trip at Golden Gai — six narrow alleys of 200+ tiny bars, each seating 6-10 people. Every bar has its own theme and personality. Some welcome tourists, some are regulars-only — look for signs in English.
details: 🍸 Cover charge ¥500-1,000 at most bars — it's normal
🎵 Themed bars: jazz, punk, cinema, 80s, horror
👶 Not kid-friendly late at night — do this as adults-only if possible
📸 The alleys themselves are photogenic even if you don't drink
🌃 Start around 8pm — by 11pm it's packed

meals.name: Omoide Yokocho Revisited
meals.description: Full circle — end where you started. Those same tiny yakitori alleys hit different after 14 days in Japan. You'll appreciate every smoky detail.

title: Sayonara Japan — Last Bites & Departure
description: Your final morning in Japan. Squeeze in last-minute shopping, grab souvenirs, and have one more incredible meal before heading to the airport. You'll be back — everyone comes back.

activities.title: Last Morning Convenience Store Run
activities.description: Japanese convenience stores are a world unto themselves. Stock up on Kit-Kat flavors (matcha, strawberry, sake), Japanese snacks, and unique drinks for the flight home and as gifts.
details: 🍫 Kit-Kat store at Tokyo Station for Japan-exclusive flavors
🛒 7-Eleven/Lawson/FamilyMart — onigiri, sandwiches, and sweets for the flight
🎁 Don Quijote for last-minute souvenirs if needed

activities.title: Tokyo Station Shopping & Departure
activities.description: Tokyo Station itself is a destination — the Marunouchi red-brick facade is gorgeous, and the underground shopping areas have every souvenir and treat imaginable.
details: 🏛️ Marunouchi exit — photograph the beautiful 1914 red-brick station building
🍰 Tokyo Banana, Shiroi Koibito, and other classic omiyage (souvenir snacks)
🧳 Ship luggage ahead with Yamato/Sagawa if you have too much — they deliver to the airport
✈️ Allow 3 hours for international flights — Narita especially

meals.name: Last Japanese Breakfast
meals.description: Find a teishoku (set meal) breakfast at the hotel or nearby: grilled fish, miso soup, rice, pickles, and tamagoyaki. The simple beauty of a Japanese breakfast — you'll miss this most.

tips.text: Tax-free shopping tip: if you spent over ¥5,000 at any single store, you likely got tax-free. Keep those receipts in your passport holder — customs may check at the airport. Also: don't open tax-free sealed bags until you leave Japan.

activities.title: Head to Airport & Fly Home
activities.description: Take the Narita Express (JR Pass) or Limousine Bus to the airport. Check in, browse duty-free for last-minute Japanese whisky or cosmetics, and reflect on 15 incredible days.
details: 🚅 Narita Express from Tokyo Station — ~1 hour, covered by JR Pass
🚌 Limousine Bus from major hotels — ~90 min, ¥3,200
🥃 Duty-free: Japanese whisky (Suntory, Nikka) and skincare are great deals
💰 Spend remaining yen at airport shops — coins can't be exchanged back
